Born and raised in [[Riviera Beach, Florida]], Gee attended the [[University of Alabama]], where he played for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball]] team for four seasons. ==High school career== Gee attended [[William T. Dwyer High School]] in [[Palm Beach Gardens, Florida]] where he led them to Class 5A state titles in 2004 and 2005. As a junior in 2003–04, he averaged 15 points and seven rebounds per game as he earned All-State Tournament team and honorable mention All-State honors. He was also awarded the Most Valuable Player of the 2004 Adidas Showcase national tournament.{{cite web|url=http://www.rolltide.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/alonzo_gee_334145.html|title=Alonzo Gee Bio|work=RollTide.com|access-date=September 5, 2014}} On November 16, 2004, he signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play [[college basketball]] for the [[University of Alabama]].{{cite web|url=http://www.rolltide.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111604aad.html|title=Alabama Signs Four Men's Basketball Players|work=RollTide.com|date=November 16, 2004|access-date=September 5, 2014}} As a senior in 2004–05, he averaged 21.3 points and 6.8 rebounds per game as was named the Class 5A State Tournament Most Valuable Player and the ''South Florida Sun-Sentinel'' Player of the Year. He also earned all-state first team honors. Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Gee was listed as the No. 10 shooting guard and the No. 33 player in the nation in 2005.{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/28630|title=Alonzo Gee Recruiting Profile|work=Rivals.com|access-date=September 5, 2014}} ==College career== In his freshman season at [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], Gee was named to the All-SEC Freshman team after averaging 8.6 points and 3.4 rebounds in 31 games. In his sophomore season, he was named the Most Valuable Player of the Paradise Jam Tournament after scoring 12 points against Middle Tennessee, 21 points against Iowa and 13 points against Xavier while shooting 54.5 percent from the field in three games as the Tide won the tournament championship. In 32 games (all starts), he averaged 12.6 points and 5.3 rebounds per game. He also scored a then career high 26 points against [[Coppin State University]]. In his junior season, he scored his 1,000th career point against Tennessee on January 29, 2008. He earned All-Tournament team honors at the Findlay Toyota Las Vegas Classic. He was also named to the All-SEC Preseason second team by the league's coaches. In 33 games (all starts), he averaged 14.5 points and 5.2 rebounds per game. In his senior season, he was named to the All-SEC second team after averaging 15.0 points and 7.2 rebounds in 32 games.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/alonzo-gee-1.html|title=Alonzo Gee Stats|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=September 5, 2014}} Gee finished his basketball career at Alabama by being one of 41 players to score 1000 points in the career, as well as 127 assists, 120 steals and 35 blocked shots. ==Professional career== ===Austin Toros (2009–2010)=== [[File:CJ Miles and Alonzo Gee.jpg|thumb|right|Gee (right) of the Washington Wizards walks next to [[C. J. Miles]] of the Utah Jazz during a game in March 2010]] After going undrafted in the [[2009 NBA draft]], Gee joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for the 2009 NBA Summer League. On September 27, 2009, he signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/training_camp_roster_2009_09_27.html|title=Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=September 27, 2009|access-date=September 5, 2014}} However, he was later waived by the Timberwolves on October 6, 2009. On November 5, 2009, he was selected with the sixth overall pick in the [[2009 NBA Development League draft|2009 NBA D-League draft]] by the [[Austin Spurs|Austin Toros]]. In 36 games (35 starts) for the Toros, he averaged 21.0 points and 6.6 rebounds per game.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/gee_signed_100307.html |title=Wizards Sign Swingman Alonzo Gee to 10-Day Contract |work=NBA.com |date=March 7, 2010 |access-date=March 29, 2010 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100321004752/http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/gee_signed_100307.html |archive-date=March 21, 2010 |url-status=live}} ===Washington Wizards (2010)=== On March 7, 2010, Gee signed a 10-day contract with the [[Washington Wizards]]. Four days later, he made his NBA debut in a game against the [[Atlanta Hawks]], recording two points and two rebounds in seven minutes of action. On March 18, 2010, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Wizards.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/gee_100318.html |title=Wizards Sign Gee to Second 10-Day Contract |work=NBA.com |date=March 18, 2010 |access-date =March 29, 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100322203404/http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/gee_100318.html| archive-date= March 22, 2010|url-status=live}} ===San Antonio Spurs (2010)=== After his second 10-day contract expired with the Wizards, on March 29, 2010, Gee signed with the San Antonio Spurs.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs_sign_alonzo_gee_100328.html |title=Spurs Sign Alonzo Gee |work=NBA.com |date=March 29, 2010 |access-date =March 30, 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100404061437/http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs_sign_alonzo_gee_100328.html| archive-date= April 4, 2010|url-status=live}} On April 8, 2010, he was assigned to the Austin Toros.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/gee_100408.html|title=Alonzo Gee Assigned To Austin Toros|work=NBA.com|date=April 8, 2010|access-date=September 5, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141122202601/http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/gee_100408.html|archive-date=November 22, 2014|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}} On April 17, 2010, he was named the 2010 NBA D-League Rookie of the Year.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/rookie_100417.html|title=Austin's Alonzo Gee Named Rookie of the Year|work=NBA.com|date=April 17, 2010|access-date=September 5, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150130105456/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/rookie_100417.html|archive-date=January 30, 2015|url-status=dead}} Six days later, he was recalled by the Spurs.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs_recall_gee_jerrells_100423.html|title=Spurs Recall Alonzo Gee and Curtis Jerrells|work=NBA.com|date=April 23, 2010|access-date=September 5, 2014}} In July 2010, he joined the Spurs for the 2010 NBA Summer League. On November 16, 2010, he was waived by the Spurs just nine games into the season.{{cite news |title=Spurs Waive Alonzo Gee |url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs_waive_alonzo_gee_101116.html
